sections.h2: Who do I call about a Hart County, KY tax bill?
sections.html:
Hart County runs its tax work from Main Street in Munfordville. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assigns each parcel a value, the sheriff takes the money, and the clerk records deeds and inherits bills that nobody paid.

  • PVA: P.O. Box 566, Munfordville, KY 42765, phone (270) 524-2321, weekday hours of 8 until 4.
  • Sheriff: 100 Main Street, phone (270) 524-2341. The county's sheriff page directs owners to hartcountysheriffky.com for online payment.
  • Clerk: 200 Main Street, phone (270) 524-2751, open weekdays 8 until 4 and Saturday mornings from 9 to noon.

State law names the sheriff as collector of state, county, school and special district taxes (KRS 134.119). The sheriff may take part payments, and a relative, tenant or lender can pay on the owner's behalf.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Hart County's land and people?
sections.html:
Hart County is cave country in south central Kentucky, and nearly nine in ten residents (88.3 percent) were counted as rural in 2020. Hardin and Barren counties gave up land to form it in 1819. It spans 418 square miles and has two cities: Munfordville, the seat, and Horse Cave, the biggest.

Underground features define the west side. Part of Mammoth Cave National Park sits there, and the Fisher Ridge Cave System, charted at roughly 125 miles in 2018, passes beneath Hart County farms. Amish families began settling between Munfordville and Horse Cave in 1989, and 2,486 people, about 12.9 percent of the county, belonged to that community in 2020.

History left a mark on paperwork. The Battle of Munfordville took place in 1862, and a January 1928 courthouse fire consumed some county records. A seller of an older farm who finds holes in the title paperwork can ask the clerk what survives for that parcel.

The 2020 census recorded 7,418 households, of which 27.4 percent were single people living alone. Of 8,816 housing units, 15.9 percent stood vacant. Wikipedia's county profile labels the northern borders with Hardin and LaRue counties as the Eastern time boundary, while Hart County itself keeps Central time, so confirm which clock your closing office follows.

sections.h2: Which counties border Hart County, and how fast has it grown?
sections.html:
Seven counties touch Hart County: Hardin and LaRue to the north, Green to the east, Metcalfe to the southeast, Barren to the south, Edmonson to the southwest and Grayson to the northwest. Each neighbor runs its own PVA and sheriff, so a seller comparing listings across a county line deals with a different office.

Hart County's population climbed from 18,199 in 2010 to 19,288 in 2020, a gain of 6.0 percent, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate of 20,117 continues the trend. With 412.56 square miles of land, density works out to 46.8 people per square mile, up from 44.2 in 2010.

sections.h2: How affordable is housing in Hart County?
sections.html:
Estimates for 2020 to 2024 show cheap housing with a strong owner base: close to three of every four homes are lived in by their owners, and values trail the state's metro areas by a wide margin.

The population rose 4.3 percent from the April 2020 base to the July 2025 estimate. Households hold 2.62 people on average, and 89.9 percent of residents had not moved in the past year. Among adults 25 and over, 81.2 percent finished high school and 12.2 percent hold a bachelor's degree. Broadband reaches 83.7 percent of households.

Employers numbered 276 in 2023 and supplied 4,073 jobs. Retail sales came to about $244.8 million in 2022, or $12,492 for every resident, and the average commute runs 28.7 minutes. The poverty rate is 18.0 percent, and 1,002 residents are veterans.

sections.h2: When is a Hart County tax bill late?
sections.html:
Everything is due by the last day of the assessment year, and KRS 134.015 adds a reward for early payers and a surcharge for late ones.

  • On or before Nov. 1: the bill shrinks 2 percent when paid whole.
  • Nov. 2 through Dec. 31: face value.
  • January: face value plus 5 percent.
  • Later: face value plus 10 percent.

The PVA can tell you who is listed as owner on January 1, since that date controls the name printed on the bill. Someone who closes in spring will probably see the first bill arrive addressed to the seller, so decide at the table who covers it.

sections.h2: What can I do if Hart County values my property too high?
sections.html:
Talk to the PVA, and if that fails, petition the county board of assessment appeals. The process sits in KRS 133.120, rewritten by the 2026 General Assembly with an effective date of July 15, 2026.

  1. Ask for a conference with the PVA or a deputy. Phone conferences are allowed on request.
  2. Still unhappy? File a petition at the clerk's office no later than one workday after the inspection period ends. State your objections, name the parcel, and give the value you think is fair.
  3. Show up at the hearing with documents: listings, comparable sales, insurance records, building cost or loan papers. A petition with no facts behind it is denied.

The board meets between 25 and 35 days after inspection ends (KRS 133.030) and visits the property when asked. Meanwhile you owe tax on the number you claimed, and the board's final number may bring a bill for the difference.

sections.h2: Can Hart County homeowners get a homestead exemption?
sections.html: Yes, for a person over 65 or totally disabled who lives in the house. The Revenue Department's deduction for 2025 and 2026 is $49,100. Against the county's $146,000 Census median, taxable value would fall to $96,900. File with the Hart County PVA, and report a sale so the deduction ends at the old address.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes when a Hart County house sells?
sections.html:
The debt stays with the land: a delinquency lien under KRS 134.420 survives a change of ownership, and a title search will turn it up.

Request a payoff from the sheriff before you list. Once claims pass to the clerk, KRS 134.119 piles a collection fee on top (ten percent of the tax plus ten percent of the penalty), and an investor may buy the certificate and add interest. Closing offers the cleanest fix: the title company deducts the payoff from your proceeds.

sections.h2: How does transfer tax work when a Hart County house sells?
sections.html: Kentucky taxes the seller at fifty cents for every $500 of value, and the clerk collects before recording the deed (KRS 142.050). At $146,000 that is $146. The clerk's office on Main Street in Munfordville holds the county's land records, so call for the current recording charge.

faqs.q: Which office mails the Hart County tax bill?
faqs.a: The sheriff, at (270) 524-2341. The PVA supplies the value, and the clerk picks up claims the sheriff could not collect.

faqs.q: How large is the homestead deduction for Hart County owners?
faqs.a: $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. It goes to owners over 65 or totally disabled who apply with the PVA at (270) 524-2321.

faqs.q: Does Hart County reward early payment?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the whole bill by November 1 cuts it 2 percent. Waiting past December 31 triggers 5 percent in January and 10 percent after that.

faqs.q: Do I stop paying while my Hart County appeal is pending?
faqs.a: No. You owe tax on your claimed value in the meantime, and a higher final value brings a supplemental bill with interest.

faqs.q: Can a Hart County house with back taxes be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien follows the parcel, so obtain a sheriff payoff and let the title company pay it from the proceeds.
